en: The Banaue Rice Terraces act as giant inclined planes, reducing the force needed for farmers to carry heavy harvests up the mountain.
Jeepney tires have deep treads to increase friction and prevent slipping on wet Philippine roads during the rainy season.
The water in Pagsanjan Falls flows rapidly downward because Earth's gravity pulls the mass of the water toward the ground.
The black sand beaches of Ilocos contain magnetite, a naturally magnetic mineral that can be picked up using a magnet.
The Makiling-Banahaw geothermal power plant in Laguna generates electricity by using steam from deep underground to spin giant turbines.
Bioluminescent plankton in the waters of Donsol, Sorsogon, produce their own blue-green light through a chemical reaction inside their bodies.
Visitors inside the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River hear distinct echoes because sound waves bounce off the hard limestone cave walls.
The natural hot springs in Los Baños, Laguna, contain water heated by geothermal energy from the underlying volcanic activity of Mount Makiling.
A falling coconut from a tall tree in Quezon province converts stored gravitational potential energy into kinetic energy as it drops.
The sharp, tapered blade of a traditional bolo acts as a wedge to split hard coconuts apart with less effort.
Filipino vendors often rub coconut oil on wooden cart wheels to reduce friction and make the pushcarts easier to roll.
Modern e-jeepneys cruising the streets of Manila use electric motors containing electromagnets to convert electrical energy into motion.
